prompt: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages about Intel Core Ultra AI acceleration.
OpenVINO optimizes model deployment across CPU, GPU, and NPU devices with runtime plugins and graph transformations.
Embedding models convert text into vectors so that semantically similar passages can be found with nearest neighbor search.
Reranking models compare a query with candidate documents and return relevance scores for each pair.
A RAG pipeline retrieves candidate passages, reranks them, and provides the strongest evidence to a generation model.
INT8 quantization can improve inference throughput by reducing memory bandwidth and model storage requirements.
NPU benchmarks often need fixed sequence lengths to avoid dynamic shape compilation issues.
GPU utilization and GPU memory utilization should be reported separately when hardware tools expose both counters.
Process RSS and system memory are useful deployment metrics but can perturb latency if sampled too aggressively.
Benchmark warm up iterations should be excluded from steady state latency and throughput averages.
Choosing an embedding maximum length requires balancing semantic coverage against latency and memory cost.
Candidate set size is one of the main scaling dimensions for text reranking workloads.
Vector search provides broad recall while reranking improves final precision for the top retrieved documents.
CPU baselines help compare model size, quantization, and plugin settings across machines.
OpenVINO compiled model cache affects startup time but should be separated from inference latency metrics.
Quality metrics such as recall at k and nDCG are separate from performance metrics such as latency and throughput.
